title: Full Revision: Humanity Amplified
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Stefan Bauschard announces the second full revision of his book Humanity Amplified, updated through July 2026, which argues that the right response to machine deep learning is to invest in human deep learning. The book explains in plain language how large language models, reasoning, and agentic AI work, then argues for education that builds mastery, identity, and creativity through real intellectual work — debate, entrepreneurship, design thinking, project-based learning, and robotics. Each revision has been necessitated by the speed of AI development: since the September 2025 edition, frontier agents can now sustain sixteen hours of expert work, an AI has produced new mathematics, and model capability has advanced dramatically. Bauschard's core thesis is that AI can do a student's retrieval but cannot do a student's developing, and schools organized around content delivery and retrieval are preparing students for work machines have already made free.
points: The central thesis: the right response to machine deep learning is human deep learning — mastery, identity, and creativity that develop when students do real intellectual work rather than complete assignments about it.
AI can perform retrieval and increasingly autonomous task completion; what it cannot replicate is a student's developing — the building of genuine capability through real stakes and real audiences.
The practices that reliably produce human deep learning include debate, project-based learning, design thinking, entrepreneurship education, robotics, and portfolio development.

The book has required two full revisions since May 2024 because AI capability now advances in months and weeks: frontier agents went from struggling with short tasks to sustaining sixteen hours of expert-level work.
Schools remain organized around delivering and retrieving content, which is precisely the work machines have now made free — making the gap between school and the economy structural, not temporary.
quotes: Machines had just learned to learn. The systems remaking the economy were not programmed with rules; they were trained on examples until capability emerged.
Schools, meanwhile, remained organized around delivering and retrieving content, which is precisely the work the machines had just made free.
